metin: Many cities are trying to reduce the number of cars in their centres. Some have closed streets to traffic at weekends, while others charge drivers a fee to enter. At first, shop owners often worry that they will lose customers. However, studies show that people who walk or cycle actually visit local shops more often.
dogru: Reducing cars in city centres can help local shops rather than harm them.
celdiriciler: Shop owners in city centres always support closing streets to cars.
Cities are building more roads so that drivers can reach the centre.
Studies show that local shops lose customers when streets are closed.

metin: When Selin started university, she found it hard to manage her time. She often left her assignments until the last night and felt stressed. A friend suggested making a weekly plan with small daily goals. Since then, Selin has finished her work earlier and feels much calmer.
dogru: Planning her week helped Selin manage her studies with less stress.
celdiriciler: Selin left university because she was stressed.
Selin's friend did her assignments for her.
Selin still does all her work on the last night.

metin: Volunteering is not only good for the community; it can also benefit the volunteers themselves. People who volunteer regularly often feel less lonely and more confident. They also learn new skills, such as teamwork and problem solving. Some even find jobs through the contacts they make.
dogru: Volunteering helps both the community and the people who volunteer.
celdiriciler: Volunteering is a good way to earn a lot of money.
People who volunteer usually feel more lonely.
Volunteers rarely learn anything useful.

metin: Our local park used to be dirty and unsafe, so few families went there. Last year, a group of neighbours decided to change this. They planted trees, painted the benches and organised weekly clean-ups. Today the park is full of children and older people every afternoon.
dogru: Neighbours worked together to turn a neglected park into a popular place.
celdiriciler: The city council built a completely new park.
The park became dirtier after the neighbours' project.
Families stopped visiting the park last year.

metin: Tourism brings money and jobs to many small towns. However, when too many visitors arrive, problems can appear. Rents go up, streets become crowded and local people may have to move away. Some towns now limit the number of tourists who can visit each day.
dogru: Tourism is useful for small towns, but too much of it can cause problems.
celdiriciler: Small towns do not earn any money from tourism.
Most towns want as many tourists as possible every day.
Tourism always makes life cheaper for local people.

metin: Mark had always wanted to live abroad, so he accepted a job in Japan. The first months were difficult because he could not speak the language and missed his family. He decided to take evening classes and joined a local hiking club. After a year, he felt at home and had many Japanese friends.
dogru: After a difficult start, Mark settled happily into his new life in Japan.
celdiriciler: Mark returned home because he could not learn Japanese.
Mark moved to Japan with his family.
Mark found life in Japan easy from the first day.

metin: Many people check their phones as soon as they wake up. Experts say this habit can make us feel stressed before the day has even started. Instead, they suggest spending the first half hour doing something calm, such as stretching or having breakfast slowly. This can improve concentration for the rest of the day.
dogru: Avoiding the phone early in the morning can help us feel calmer and focus better.
celdiriciler: Experts recommend reading the news on the phone right after waking up.
Having breakfast slowly makes people more stressed.
Checking the phone in the morning improves concentration.

metin: The school canteen used to sell mostly chips, burgers and fizzy drinks. After parents complained, the school changed the menu. Now there are salads, soups and fresh fruit every day. At first some students were unhappy, but most of them now say they feel less tired in the afternoon.
dogru: A healthier school menu was introduced and most students now like it.
celdiriciler: The school stopped selling food completely.
Students asked for more burgers and fizzy drinks.
Parents wanted the canteen to sell more chips.

metin: Recycling is important, but it is not the only way to reduce waste. Buying fewer things and repairing old ones can make an even bigger difference. For example, a phone that is used for four years instead of two creates much less waste. Some towns now have free repair cafés where volunteers help people fix things.
dogru: Using things longer and repairing them can reduce waste more than recycling alone.
celdiriciler: Recycling is the only way to reduce waste.
People should buy a new phone every year.
Repair cafés charge a lot of money to fix things.

metin: Ece was nervous about giving a presentation in front of her class. She practised in front of a mirror and then with her brother. On the day, her hands were shaking at first, but she remembered to breathe slowly. In the end, her teacher said it was one of the best presentations.
dogru: Ece prepared carefully and gave a successful presentation despite her nerves.
celdiriciler: Ece refused to give her presentation.
Ece's brother gave the presentation for her.
Ece was completely relaxed and did not need to practise.

metin: Working from home has become common since the pandemic. Many employees enjoy not having to travel and being able to organise their own day. However, some find it hard to separate work from free time. Companies are now experimenting with mixed systems, where people spend part of the week in the office.
dogru: Working from home has advantages and disadvantages, so many companies mix it with office work.
celdiriciler: All companies have stopped letting people work from home.
Everyone finds it easy to separate work and free time at home.
Working from home became less common after the pandemic.

metin: Bees are essential for growing many of the fruits and vegetables we eat. In recent years, the number of bees has fallen in many countries. Scientists believe that pesticides, disease and the loss of wild flowers are the main causes. People can help by planting flowers and avoiding chemicals in their gardens.
dogru: Bees are declining for several reasons, and people can take simple steps to help them.
celdiriciler: The number of bees is growing quickly all over the world.
Bees have no effect on the food we eat.
Scientists say that planting flowers kills bees.

metin: When Burak failed his driving test for the second time, he almost gave up. His instructor told him that many good drivers fail at first because of nerves. They practised the parts he found difficult, especially parking. On his third attempt, Burak passed without any mistakes.
dogru: With extra practice, Burak passed his driving test after two failures.
celdiriciler: Burak passed his driving test the first time.
Burak decided never to drive again.
Burak's instructor told him he would never be a good driver.

metin: Reading for pleasure has many benefits for children. It improves their vocabulary and helps them understand other people's feelings. Unfortunately, many children now spend more time on screens than with books. Some schools have started a daily fifteen-minute reading time to encourage the habit.
dogru: Reading for pleasure helps children, and some schools are trying to encourage it.
celdiriciler: Children today read more books than ever before.
Reading has no effect on children's vocabulary.
Schools have banned reading time to allow more screen time.

metin: A small café in our town decided to stop using plastic cups. Customers who bring their own cup now get a discount. At first, only a few people did it, but the idea quickly became popular. Now other cafés on the same street are doing the same thing.
dogru: A café's plan to reduce plastic spread to other cafés.
celdiriciler: The café started using more plastic cups.
Customers had to pay more if they brought their own cup.
The idea failed because nobody brought a cup.

metin: Learning a musical instrument as an adult is harder than as a child, but it is not impossible. Adults usually have less free time and can be more afraid of making mistakes. On the other hand, they are often better at planning their practice. Many teachers say adult students make steady progress if they practise a little every day.
dogru: Adults can learn an instrument successfully, although they face some difficulties.
celdiriciler: Adults can never learn to play an instrument.
Adults learn instruments faster than children in every way.
Teachers say adults should practise only once a month.

metin: Last winter, heavy snow cut off a mountain village for five days. The roads were closed and there was no electricity. The villagers shared food and wood and checked on older neighbours every morning. When the road was finally cleared, nobody had been seriously hurt.
dogru: Villagers helped each other through several days of isolation caused by snow.
celdiriciler: The village was cut off by a flood in summer.
Many villagers were seriously hurt during the storm.
The villagers left the village before the snow came.

metin: Online reviews can be very useful when choosing a hotel or restaurant. However, not all reviews are honest. Some businesses pay people to write positive comments, while others receive unfair negative ones. It is a good idea to read many reviews and look for details rather than just stars.
dogru: Online reviews are helpful but should be read carefully because some are not honest.
celdiriciler: All online reviews are completely honest.
It is best to look only at the number of stars.
Businesses are not allowed to receive reviews online.

metin: Gamze always wanted to open her own bakery, but she was afraid of the risk. She kept her office job and started selling cakes to friends at weekends. As more people ordered, she realised there was real demand. Two years later, she left her job and opened a small shop.
dogru: Gamze tested her bakery idea slowly before opening her own shop.
celdiriciler: Gamze opened a bakery immediately after school.
Gamze's cakes were unpopular, so she kept her office job.
Gamze works in someone else's bakery at weekends.

metin: Many people believe that drinking coffee is bad for health. In fact, recent research suggests that moderate amounts, around two or three cups a day, may have some benefits. However, too much coffee can cause problems with sleep and make people nervous. As with most things, the key is not to overdo it.
dogru: Moderate coffee drinking may be fine, but too much can cause problems.
celdiriciler: Coffee is always very harmful to health.
Drinking ten cups of coffee a day is recommended.
Coffee helps everyone sleep better.

metin: In some countries, students take a gap year between school and university. They might travel, work or volunteer abroad. Supporters say that this experience helps young people become more independent and decide what they really want to study. Critics, however, worry that some students lose the habit of studying.
dogru: A gap year can help students grow, although some people have concerns about it.
celdiriciler: All universities require students to take a gap year.
Students on a gap year always stop studying forever.
A gap year means studying two subjects at the same time.

metin: Kerem noticed that his elderly neighbour rarely left her flat. He started visiting her once a week to bring shopping and have a chat. Over time, she told him stories about the history of the neighbourhood. Kerem says these visits have become one of the best parts of his week.
dogru: Kerem's visits to his lonely neighbour turned into a friendship he values.
celdiriciler: Kerem's neighbour helps him with his shopping every week.
Kerem moved in with his elderly neighbour.
Kerem found the visits boring and stopped going.

metin: Fast fashion allows people to buy trendy clothes at very low prices. But producing so many clothes uses huge amounts of water and energy. Many items are worn only a few times before they are thrown away. Some shoppers are now choosing second-hand clothes to reduce this waste.
dogru: Cheap fashion has an environmental cost, so some people buy second-hand clothes instead.
celdiriciler: Fast fashion uses very little water and energy.
Most cheap clothes are worn for many years.
Second-hand clothes are becoming less popular.

metin: The city museum was losing visitors because young people found it boring. The new director decided to change the way exhibitions were presented. She added interactive screens, evening events with music and guided tours led by students. In one year, the number of young visitors doubled.
dogru: Changes made by a new director attracted more young people to the museum.
celdiriciler: The museum closed because nobody visited it.
The new director removed all the modern screens.
Young visitors decreased after the changes.

metin: Some parents give their children pocket money every week. Experts say this can teach children how to manage money if it is done well. Children learn to save for things they want and to accept that money is limited. The important thing is that parents do not immediately give more when the money runs out.
dogru: Pocket money can teach children about managing money if parents are consistent.
celdiriciler: Experts say children should never receive money.
Parents should give more money whenever children ask.
Pocket money makes children worse at saving.

metin: Before the invention of the fridge, people had to find other ways to keep food fresh. They dried meat and fish, kept vegetables in cool cellars and made jam from fruit. In winter, some people collected ice from lakes and stored it under straw. These methods allowed families to have food all year round.
dogru: Before fridges, people used several methods to preserve food.
celdiriciler: Before fridges, people could not keep any food fresh.
People used fridges to make jam in the past.
Ice was only used to make cold drinks.

metin: Our company introduced a four-day working week as an experiment. Employees worked slightly longer hours on the other days but had Fridays off. After six months, the managers noticed that fewer people were ill and that work was completed on time. The company has now decided to keep the new system.
dogru: A four-day week experiment was successful, so the company kept it.
celdiriciler: The company stopped the experiment because work was late.
Employees had to work every day of the week.
More people were ill during the experiment.

metin: Many teenagers feel pressure to look perfect on social media. They compare themselves with carefully edited photos and feel unhappy with their own lives. Some schools now teach students how images are changed and how to think critically about what they see online. Teachers say this helps students feel more confident.
dogru: Schools are helping teenagers deal with the pressure caused by social media images.
celdiriciler: Teenagers today feel no pressure from social media.
Schools teach students how to edit their photos to look perfect.
Social media photos always show real life.

metin: Hasan wanted to lose weight, so he tried a strict diet he found online. For two weeks he ate almost nothing but salad and felt tired all the time. Then he visited a dietician, who helped him plan balanced meals. He lost weight more slowly, but he felt healthy and kept it off.
dogru: Hasan found that a balanced plan worked better for him than a strict diet.
celdiriciler: Hasan's strict online diet was the best solution for him.
Hasan gained weight after visiting the dietician.
The dietician told Hasan to eat only salad.

metin: Night trains were popular in Europe many years ago but slowly disappeared as cheap flights became common. Recently, however, they are returning. More travellers want to avoid the pollution caused by flying, and sleeping on a train saves the cost of a hotel. Several new routes have opened in the last few years.
dogru: Night trains are becoming popular again for environmental and practical reasons.
celdiriciler: Night trains have never been popular in Europe.
Night trains are disappearing because of new routes.
Travellers choose night trains because flying is cleaner.

metin: At first, Lara did not want to join the school theatre group because she was shy. Her best friend persuaded her to come to one rehearsal. She was given a small part and slowly became more comfortable on stage. By the end of the year, she had the main role in the school play.
dogru: Joining the theatre group helped shy Lara gain confidence.
celdiriciler: Lara was never interested in the theatre group.
Lara's best friend got the main role instead of her.
Lara left the theatre group after one rehearsal.

metin: Smart watches can count steps, measure heart rate and even check sleep. For many users, seeing these numbers is a good motivation to move more. However, doctors warn that the devices are not always accurate. They should not replace a proper medical check when someone feels unwell.
dogru: Smart watches can motivate people, but they cannot replace a doctor.
celdiriciler: Smart watches are always completely accurate.
Doctors say smart watches are better than medical checks.
Smart watches make people move less.

metin: In the past, most people stayed in the same job for their whole lives. Today it is common to change jobs several times, and sometimes even to change careers completely. This gives people more chances to find work they enjoy. However, it also means they need to keep learning new skills.
dogru: People change jobs more often today, which brings both chances and the need to keep learning.
celdiriciler: Most people today stay in one job for their whole lives.
Changing jobs means people never need new skills.
In the past, people changed careers very often.

metin: The village school had only twelve pupils and was going to close. The families were worried because the nearest school was an hour away by bus. They started a campaign, invited journalists and offered to help with repairs. In the end, the council agreed to keep the school open.
dogru: Families successfully campaigned to save their small village school.
celdiriciler: The village school closed and the pupils moved away.
The council built a new school next to the village.
The families wanted the school to close.

metin: Many people think that talking to plants helps them grow. Scientists are not sure about this, but some experiments suggest that vibrations from sound may have a small effect. What is certain is that people who talk to their plants usually pay more attention to them. They water them regularly and notice problems earlier.
dogru: Talking to plants may not help directly, but it often means people take better care of them.
celdiriciler: Scientists have proved that plants understand human speech.
People who talk to their plants usually forget to water them.
Sound always makes plants grow twice as fast.

metin: Onur and his wife decided to spend one weekend a month without any screens. No phones, no TV and no computers from Saturday morning to Sunday evening. At first they felt bored, but soon they started walking, cooking together and reading again. They say these weekends have improved their relationship.
dogru: Screen-free weekends helped Onur and his wife spend better time together.
celdiriciler: Onur and his wife watch more TV at weekends now.
The screen-free weekends made the couple argue more.
Onur and his wife stopped the experiment after one weekend.

metin: Wild animals are increasingly seen in cities. Foxes, raccoons and even wild boars look for food in rubbish bins. Some people enjoy seeing them, but others worry about safety and damage. Experts advise residents to close their bins properly and never feed the animals.
dogru: Wild animals are coming into cities, and people are advised not to attract them.
celdiriciler: Wild animals are disappearing from cities completely.
Experts recommend feeding wild animals in the city.
Everyone is happy to see wild boars in their streets.

metin: When Nora's grandmother moved into a care home, she left behind a large collection of old recipes. Nora decided to try cooking one every week. She took photos of the dishes and showed them to her grandmother on her visits. The project brought them closer, and Nora now plans to publish a small family cookbook.
dogru: Cooking her grandmother's recipes brought Nora closer to her grandmother.
celdiriciler: Nora's grandmother taught cooking classes in the care home.
Nora threw away her grandmother's old recipes.
Nora's grandmother cooked a dish for her every week.

metin: A new law in our country requires restaurants to show the number of calories on their menus. Supporters believe it will help people make healthier choices. Restaurant owners, on the other hand, say it is expensive to calculate the calories for every dish. It is still too early to know how much the law will change people's habits.
dogru: A new calorie law has supporters and critics, and its effect is not yet clear.
celdiriciler: Restaurants are now forbidden to sell high-calorie food.
Everyone agrees that the new law is cheap and easy for restaurants.
The law has already changed everyone's eating habits.

metin: Many people find it hard to save money at the end of the month. One simple method is to move a small amount into a savings account on the day you get paid. Because the money is no longer in your main account, you are less likely to spend it. Over a year, even small amounts can add up to a useful sum.
dogru: Saving a little as soon as you get paid is an easy way to build savings.
celdiriciler: It is best to save money only at the end of the month.
Small savings never make a real difference.
Moving money to a savings account makes people spend more.

metin: The school decided to plant a vegetable garden behind the sports hall. Each class is responsible for one part of it. Students learn about plants in science lessons and use the vegetables in cooking lessons. Teachers say that children who normally do not like vegetables are happy to eat the ones they grew themselves.
dogru: A school garden helps students learn and makes them more willing to eat vegetables.
celdiriciler: The school replaced its garden with a new sports hall.
Students buy vegetables for their cooking lessons at the supermarket.
Children refuse to eat the vegetables from the garden.

metin: Airports are among the busiest places in the world, but few travellers think about the people who keep them running. Hundreds of workers clean the planes, check the luggage and guide the aircraft on the ground. Many of them work at night so that flights can leave on time in the morning. Without them, air travel would be impossible.
dogru: Many unseen workers are needed to keep airports running.
celdiriciler: Airports are quiet places that need very few workers.
All airport workers are pilots.
Airport workers never work at night.

metin: Emma used to buy lunch every day near her office. She calculated that she was spending almost two hundred euros a month. She started preparing simple meals at home the evening before. Now she saves money and says her lunches are also healthier.
dogru: Emma saves money and eats better by preparing her own lunches.
celdiriciler: Emma spends more on lunch now than before.
Emma's office provides free lunch.
Emma stopped eating lunch to save money.

metin: Solar panels are becoming cheaper every year. In sunny countries, many families have installed them on their roofs to produce their own electricity. Although the initial cost is still quite high, the panels usually pay for themselves within a few years. Some governments also offer financial help to encourage people to buy them.
dogru: Solar panels are becoming more affordable and can save families money over time.
celdiriciler: Solar panels are getting more expensive every year.
Solar panels never save families any money.
Governments have banned solar panels on houses.

metin: Cem joined a language exchange where he meets an English student once a week. They spend half the time speaking Turkish and half speaking English. Cem says he has learned more everyday expressions than in years of classes. He has also made a good friend.
dogru: A language exchange helped Cem improve his English and make a friend.
celdiriciler: Cem teaches English at a language school.
Cem and his partner speak only English.
Cem learned fewer expressions than in his classes.

metin: Hospitals in some countries now use dogs to visit patients. The dogs are specially trained to be calm and gentle. Studies show that spending time with them can reduce stress and even pain. Children and older patients especially look forward to these visits.
dogru: Trained dogs visiting hospitals can help patients feel better.
celdiriciler: Dogs are not allowed in any hospital.
Hospital dogs make patients more stressed.
The dogs are trained to guard the hospital.

metin: Last summer, a heatwave hit the city for almost two weeks. Temperatures rose above forty degrees, and many older people had health problems. The city opened cool public spaces in libraries and shopping centres. Officials say they will prepare better plans because such heatwaves are likely to become more common.
dogru: A dangerous heatwave made the city prepare for similar events in the future.
celdiriciler: The city closed its libraries during the heatwave.
Officials believe heatwaves will become rare.
The heatwave lasted only one afternoon.

metin: Many young people dream of becoming famous online. They create videos and hope that one of them will go viral. In reality, only a very small number of creators earn enough to live on. Most spend many hours every week working on content without being paid.
dogru: Becoming a successful online creator is much harder than many young people think.
celdiriciler: Most online creators earn a lot of money quickly.
Young people are not interested in becoming famous online.
Making online videos takes very little time.

metin: After retiring, Mr Aksoy felt that he had nothing to do. His daughter suggested that he teach the neighbourhood children how to play chess. He started with three children in his living room. Now he runs a small chess club at the community centre with over thirty members.
dogru: Teaching chess gave Mr Aksoy a new purpose after he retired.
celdiriciler: Mr Aksoy learned to play chess after retiring.
Mr Aksoy's daughter runs the chess club.
The chess club closed because nobody came.

metin: Noise is one of the most common complaints in big cities. Traffic, construction and loud neighbours can disturb sleep and increase stress. Some cities have created quiet zones where noise is limited at certain times. Others encourage people to plant trees, which can reduce noise as well as clean the air.
dogru: Cities are trying different ways to reduce the harmful effects of noise.
celdiriciler: Noise has no effect on people's health.
Cities encourage more construction to reduce noise.
Trees make city streets louder.
